mark: Its 1,000-step TP lockstep screen shows 0 rank mismatches on the image; the sampled suite completes
evidence: README 3.1 pytest suite (6 files) on the candidate image, two boots; README 3.2 screen_zero_broadcast_sync.py --worker at TP3 and TP4, adapted to sp8's single GB10 (see adaptations), two boots in the PR orchestrator's order (boot1 TP3 then TP4, boot2 TP4 then TP3)
adaptations: The PR's orchestrator ssh-es to sp5..sp8 and takes their locks, so it was not run; only its --worker entry point was run, on sp8 alone, with the worker's own docker flags and NCCL/Gloo env
world_size=1 is not possible: sparknet's RoCE all-reduce rejects world size 1 (screen-tp1-smoke-*.txt)

Two ranks in two containers on one GPU: NCCL 2.30.7 refuses ('Multiple Ranks are using the same GPU/Partition. Set NCCL_MULTI_RANK_GPU_ENABLE=1', screen-tp2-one-gpu-rank*.txt). With NCCL_MULTI_RANK_GPU_ENABLE=1 and one container per rank, init fails with 'invalid device context' (screen-candidate48-boot*-tp*-onegpu-rank*.txt)

Accepted layout: every rank a separate process in ONE container, NCCL_MULTI_RANK_GPU_ENABLE=1 (pr-980-onecontainer-tp34.sh). Each rank still has its own process-global np.random state, which is what the screen's control arm desyncs, so the mismatch counts are meaningful. Its latency records are not comparable to the PR's multi-node ones (the RoCE one-shot arm loops back through the NIC at 4.5-9.2 ms per call)

parts.part: 1,000-step TP lockstep screen shows 0 rank mismatches on the image
parts.detail: TP3 and TP4, both boots: all three candidate modes 0/1000 mismatches in draft, confidence, budget, capacities, dead-cut, sampled and estimator histories, while the control arm reproduces the PR's divergence exactly. Run with all ranks on one GB10 (adapted layout), not across sp5..sp8
the sampled suite is a live tp4-switched serving benchmark

verdict_scope: sp8-evaluable part only, on an adapted single-GPU rank layout; the sampled suite is cannot-evaluate-on-sp8
reason: On the integrated image the screen's three candidate modes show 0 cross-rank mismatches over 1,000 steps at TP3 and TP4 in both boots, and the control arm reproduces the PR's recorded divergence value for value, so the lockstep seeding and zero-broadcast confidence path hold. Caveats: the ranks shared one GPU (NCCL_MULTI_RANK_GPU_ENABLE=1, one container), not the PR's multi-node layout; and at TP2, a world size the PR did not claim, the candidate_sampled_unseeded mode hit an illegal memory access in rejection_sample twice. That TP2 crash may be an artifact of the shared-GPU layout or of the screen's TP2 shapes (vocab 8192), but it is unexplained and worth a look before trusting temperature > 0 at TP2.
notes: commands.txt start_utc is when the command was issued and includes any wait on /tmp/spark-lab-gpu.lock
The screen was not run on the 1107 image: its control arm is the PR's built-in model of 1107's seeding, and the PR compared against that arm, not against the 1107 image
